questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had never been there before and everyone spoke well of the city, and there were many exchange spots, and it is cheap :)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy! The faculty of humanities was very good at sharing information by email before the semester started and in the intro week.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We got 5 days of introduction about uni stuff, information about the city, the country, it's traditions, places to visit and where to go in Prague

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found my housing on facebook and it was not too hard. I lived with people who were not students so we did not do that much together, but many of my friends found housing through a website called
https://erasmusinprague.com/
which was a bit expensive but nice and then you live with other students which is a good way to get to know people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it would have been great to live with other Erasmus students that are on the same page as you and live the same lifestyle. Also look out for scammers on facebook!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was a add-and-drop period for Erasmus students which allowed you to try some courses and then drop them if you didn't like them or add new ones that you heard good things about or something. It was very useful, but also made the process harder since they had so many good courses available AND because you can choose from all faculties to some extent.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus coordinator was always good at helping. She would answer very fast and was so helpful!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, I got all the classes I chose in the preregistration, but then I changed them up a bit in the add and drop. I am very happy and content with my courses!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't look too much, just make a decision and stick with it. There are so many cool courses so you can keep looking forever. But also pick some cool ones if you can! And be quick in the preregistration period and register for too many and drop out rather than too few and be in trouble later.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took a vide variety of courses. They were all interesting and very different. Some had lectures, som had seminars. Some had a lot of readings and projects over the semester, but others only had a final exam.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It varied so much. Most of the courses had more projects throughout the semester than in UCPH and therefore less stressful final exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Czech language course for beginners
Introduction to brain
Feminism and environmental movements
Gender and religion
Can I hate God?
Ancient mysteries and the environment
Music and space/place

And Yoga for fun

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Introduction to brain!! And the sports courses. They were not accepted in the preapproval but still fun to participate in.
Also the Gender and religion course I enjoyed a lot.

questions.answer: Nothing I can remember

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Alcohol less expensive. Coffee more expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could join the sport courses and the introweek which were both very fun.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sports and introweek

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of good techno/electronic clubs, concerts of all kinds of music, and events going on all the time. Also easy to take a bus to another city or country, and pretty cheap.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I did not get to know a lot of Czech friends except one girl that showed us around during the intro week. The courses I took had mainly Erasmus students in them, and the Czech students would mostly talk to other Czech students. Outside of school I experienced the same. Czech people didn't really talk to me that much, I met mostly international people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them before or after class I guess.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I felt like the Czechs were not very talkative and kept mostly to them selves, and I wish I had met more of local people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their Beer :P and their cute houses and beautiful city. I love the parks, Riegrovy Sady has the best view of Prague.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Get social on the first day of introweek/uni!!!! People are so ready to meet and make friends and for me it was important to make use of that day. I made most of my friends on the first day of introweek.
2. Do something everyday. The time runs away so fast that even though I was tired I tried to do at least a little bit of sightseeing, go to a new cafe/bar, go to some events or something, just do something small (or big) everyday.
3. Don't worry too much about school. It will be fine.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't remember anything right now. Just enjoy every moment.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting my friends!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The shooting at the faculty of arts was a huge challenge, and of course very unexpected.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
